junk_imagery.evidence: No photos or AI images anywhere. Every frame from hook@0.3 to payoff@-0.4 is flat vector chart art plus the mascot.

decorative_mascot.evidence: At seg2:start/mid/end Data stands beside the 24.8K and 430K numbers and points; he does nothing to them. At seg3:mid/end he just perches on the 56 bubble. At seg4:mid through payoff@-0.4 he stands on a ladder pointing at the hourglass instead of flipping it or pouring the sand. Only the hook ladder and the seg1 timeline walk tie him to the number at all.

bare_number_card.evidence: seg2:start-end is two big numbers, 24.8K and 430K, in two rows with a mascot beside each. There is no race, no distance and no visible 17x gap; the numbers alone carry the comparison.

dead_air.evidence: Code measured longest_static_s=0.0. Every segment has something moving: bars grow, the timeline is walked, the bubbles grow, the sand falls.

empty_void.evidence: Dark ground but no large dead area; dark_fraction=0.0. seg1:start is sparse in its upper-right, but it fills as the bars arrive.

unreadable.evidence: In seg4:start through payoff@-0.4 the ladder's rail runs through the label 'New York to Tokyo', so it reads 'Ne  York'. At seg3:end the '56' inside the yellow bubble is double-printed into an illegible blob.

weakest_scene.visible_evidence: seg2:start-end: two text rows, 'Apollo 10 -- fastest humans ever traveled (1969) 24.8K' and 'Parker Solar Probe (2024) 430K', each with a Data standing beside it. A dotted vertical line sits at the right edge. Nothing shows that one is 17 times the other.
weakest_scene.root_cause: The comparison was drawn as a pair of number cards instead of a picture where the ratio is visible as distance or motion, so the '17 times faster' claim is only stated in text.
weakest_scene.repair_goal: Make the 17x visible as a race. Apollo 10 and Parker each streak across the frame toward the same line: in the time the capsule covers 1 unit, the probe covers 17 and blows past the frame edge. Data should be the cause, for example lighting or launching the probe, not standing beside a label. Keep one headline number.

depictions.note: Plain bar chart of record speeds with sun icons. Data climbs a ladder to raise the 2024 bar, but it is still bars.
Timeline spike chart. Data walks the axis while a counter ticks up to 430,000. It is a line chart with a walker.
Two lanes of numbers with a mascot in each and no vehicles. Nothing shows 17x.
Two sized bubbles, 56 and 208. A bubble chart, not a trip from New York to Tokyo or around the Earth.
Stock hourglass pair with the sand falling. Generic timer, and it ignores the 'diving into the sun' closing line.

grades.one_line: A chart-led explainer: bars, a timeline, number cards, bubbles and hourglasses, with the 17x and 56-second claims never shown physically and Data mostly pointing.
problems: Hook (hook@0.3 to seg0:end) is a slow bar-chart build titled 'Fastest thing built', with no speed, motion or probe on screen.
seg2 is a bare number card, 24.8K vs 430K, and the 17x comparison is never visualised.
seg3 is a bubble chart. The '56' glyph is garbled at seg3:end, and 'NEW YORK TO TOKYO SITS LOWEST' is chart-speak.
In seg4 the ladder covers the 'New York to Tokyo' label, and the hourglass is a generic timer. The closing 'diving straight into the sun' has no visual at all.
Data points or perches in seg2, seg3 and seg4 instead of causing the motion.
There is no probe, no sun and no Earth anywhere in a video about a solar probe.
fixes: Open on the probe itself streaking toward the sun with a speedometer reading 430K mph, and make Data the one throwing the throttle.
Turn seg2 into a race: an Apollo capsule against the probe over the same time, with the probe covering 17 times the distance.
Turn seg3 into a globe, with the probe crossing from New York to Tokyo in a 56-second sweep and circling Earth in 208, and Data riding or launching it.
Move the ladder off the labels, and fix the double-drawn 56 so it reads cleanly.
End on the probe diving into the sun so the closing line is shown on screen.
